rationale: Evidence. Iteration 6 (kp 2.0, kd 0.3, base_speed 1.1, narrow five-sensor array) is the best raced design at 354.2, with 16 of 20 oval finishes, oval line_loss_events 0.85 and oval max_error 0.048. Iteration 7 changed only kd (0.3 to 0.25) and fell to 163.3, with oval completion dropping to 1 of 20 and oval line loss rising to 1.3. So kd 0.3 stays. Iteration 8's pending candidate (base_speed 1.2) is not supported: iteration 1 at 1.3 and iteration 4 at 1.1 show line loss rising with speed, and iteration 5 at 0.9 also hurt. The Evaluator's revision request is followed. This candidate restores base_speed to 1.1, keeps kd 0.3, ki 0, last_direction and the narrow geometry, and changes kp alone from 2.0 to 1.8. The step follows the direction that cut line loss from kp 2.5 to 2.0 (oval line loss 0.95 to 0.85, max_error 0.054 to 0.048, s-bend line loss 1.25 to 1.1). Expected result: oval line_loss_events and max_error at or below the iteration 6 levels (0.85 and 0.048), oval completion at or above about 80%, and some gain on the s-bend (line loss 1.1) and slalom (line loss 1.0). Risk: kp 1.8 may be too weak to correct the tightest bends, which would raise max_error. If that happens, the next revision should return to kp 2.0 and keep speed at 1.1. Hypotheses: (a) further kp reduction continues to cut over-correction-driven line loss; (b) the s-bend and slalom failures are line loss at the bends, not sensor coverage. Measurements requested are per-track completion, progress, completion_time, line_loss_events, max_error and steering_oscillation, so the kp effect can be read against the iteration 6 baseline.
